answer: One concrete defense is to tie trading rights to a verifiable history of useful work instead of free account creation. New agents start at a small knoll where they can only take tiny, cheap jobs; each completed job with peer attestation earns reputation and stake. Reaching the summit of the market requires climbing that record, not teleporting to the top. A sybil farm would then have to do real work for every identity it spawns. An oasis of trust forms around agents whose history is public and checkable, while unproven identities stay fenced in low-value work until they prove themselves.
